          WSL Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer's Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Oliver King / Author, Jordan Collins / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our WSL match predictions for Matchday 7 of the 2026-27 season.
Manchester City could extend their perfect start to the Women’s Super League season when they face rivals Manchester United in the blockbuster clash of Matchday 7.
Another derby in north London starts the weekend's action as Tottenham look to get back to winning ways against fellow strugglers Arsenal.
Brighton host West Ham in the other match on Saturday, before unbeaten Chelsea travel to Crystal Palace in Sunday's early kick-off.
Birmingham City and Charlton Athletic go head-to-head as they both look to escape the relegation zone, while Everton welcome Aston Villa to Goodison Park.
Alexia Putellas and the London City Lionesses face Liverpool, before the Manchester derby rounds off the weekend.
Here's how the Opta supercomputer predicts MD7 of the WSL will unfold in what promises to be an exciting round of fixtures.
Tottenham have lost two of their last four WSL home games against Arsenal (W1 D1), drawing 0-0 in this fixture last season, and do not go into this derby in particularly great shape.
After going unbeaten in their first four league games this season (W3 D1), Spurs have lost 6-1 to London City and 6-2 to Chelsea in their last two games.
Indeed, Spurs are only the second team in WSL history to concede six or more goals in back-to-back games, after Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2013.
And the Opta supercomputer has predicted them to falter again, as they won just 21.6% of the pre-match simulations and clinched a draw in 21.8%.
Arsenal are winless in their last four games across all competitions (D2 L2) but have a 56.6% win probability here.
The Gunners have won 10 of their 13 north London derbies in the WSL (D2 L1), scoring five goals in their last two wins: 5-0 in February 2025, 5-2 in March 2026.
Arsenal will be keen to see Alessia Russo return to her best; she has scored more WSL goals against Spurs (eight) than any other opponent.
Just one point separates ninth-place West Ham and 12th-place Brighton, and the Seagulls have been backed by the Opta supercomputer to claim only their second league win of the season.
Brighton have been given a 50.4% chance of victory to the Hammers' 24.5%, with the probability of a draw coming in at 25.1%.

Brighton have scored seven goals across their last two league games, more than in their seven prior (six) – the Seagulls could score 2+ goals in three consecutive WSL matches in the same season for the first time.
And after losing their first two WSL home games against West Ham, Brighton have since won five of six home meetings with the Hammers in the top flight (L1).
However, West Ham have won four of their nine WSL away games in 2026 (L5), as many away victories as they managed across 2023 (two), 2024 (one) and 2025 (one) combined.
This is the fourth successive WSL season Chelsea have started with an unbeaten run of at least six, and the third in a row that they have conceded exactly three times after six matches.
